# Getting Started with RStudio {#sec-getting-started-with-rstudio}

*(Source materials: Posit's official RStudio IDE user guide — see [Resources](resources.qmd).)*

If you've just installed R for the first time in [Rubric
9](09-getting-started-with-r.qmd), this page is the natural next step. RStudio is not R
itself — it's an **integrated development environment (IDE)**: a window around R that
adds a code editor, a file browser, a plot viewer and a few dozen conveniences, so you
rarely need R's own plain console. Every code example elsewhere in this module assumes
you're working in RStudio (or [Positron](https://positron.posit.co/), its newer sibling
from the same company) rather than R's bare console.

::: {.callout-important}
Install R itself first (see [Rubric 9](09-getting-started-with-r.qmd)) — RStudio needs an
existing R installation to run and is useless without one.
:::

## Installing RStudio

Download **RStudio Desktop** (the free, open-source edition) from
[posit.co](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) and install it the same way as any
other application. When you open it for the first time, RStudio automatically detects the
R installation from Rubric 9 and uses it in the background — you won't normally interact
with plain R directly again.

## Finding Your Way Around

The official **[Posit RStudio IDE User Guide](https://docs.posit.co/ide/user/)** covers
RStudio's layout (its four panes: Source, Console, Environment/History and
Files/Plots/Packages/Help), Projects and keyboard shortcuts in much more depth than this
short page could. Treat it as your reference whenever something in the interface is
unfamiliar.
